title: Dashboard rollback debugging script and trace notes
body:
Purpose: quick, operator-friendly script for debugging dashboard-driven rollbacks (model rollouts, dashboard-led feature toggles, metric regressions). This is meant to be short-form — copyable into oncall Slack, and used during postmortem prep. Not exhaustive; annotated with trace anchors and low-cost probe suggestions.

When to use (examples):
- New model variant rollout triggered an immediate increase in latency p95 or token-level timeouts.
- Dashboard alert fired on perceived-latency SLI + user-facing error rate after a rollout.
- Canary synthetic probe flapped after configuration change (batching/kv-cache change).

Quick triage script (operator):
1) Confirm the scope: check alert context + timeseries window (alert start time T0).
   - Which tenants affected? (dashboard panel drilldown by customer_id/tenant_tag)
   - What routes/models were active at T0? (route/model filter on the route-level panel)
2) Snapshot: take a 5‑minute timeline around T0, export top 3 correlated metrics:
   - overall request rate (rps), success_rate, p95 latency, token_generation_rate, batch_size_avg
   - model_fallback_count, kvcache_hit_rate, queue_depth_per_host
3) Isolate resource contention: check GPU utilization + host queue depth. If host queue depth spikes before latency, probable queuing/backpressure.
4) Quick rollback decision criteria: if (p95 latency increase > 2x baseline AND error_rate increased > 0.5%) then consider immediate rollback to previous model variant and open rollback_incident ticket.

Low-cost probes to run immediately (scriptable):
- Synthetic sample: re-run 5 synthetic probes to the canary route with identical payloads used in canary. Compare token latency and outputs to baseline.
- Probe for KV cache warmth: run a prefix-heavy probe (same user/session seed) and measure kvcache_hit_rate at model instance level.
- Instrumented single-request trace: trigger a debug request with trace sampling forced=1 for one of affected tenants. Collect spans and link to the incident.

Trace anchoring patterns (what to look for in spans):
- span.name contains "runtime:token-loop" and shows steep slope in token iteration duration around T0.
- "batch-manager:dispatch" spans with high wait_us (sign of batching backlog).
- "kv-cache:lookup" spans with high error/retry counts (could indicate cache misconfig or eviction storm).
- "fallback-router" span occurrences (counts of fallback decision points).

Dashboard slices to inspect (panel checklist):
- Model-level panels: p50/p95/p99 token latency by model_version, side-by-side baseline vs new variant.
- Route-level panels: request_success_rate, user_visible_error_rate, avg_response_tokens.
- Autoscaling/host panels: GPU_utilization_90pct, host_queue_depth, preemption_events, container_restarts.
- Cost panels: synthetic_probe_cost, query_cost_estimate (to decide if probes will be expensive).

SQL/metric snippets (promql-friendly pseudo queries to paste):
- p95 token latency for model X: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(token_latency_bucket{model=\"X\"}[5m])) by (le))
- batch wait time per host: avg_over_time(batch_manager_wait_ms{host=\"\"}[5m])
- kv cache hit rate: sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_lookups_total[5m]))

Trace sampling guidance:
- For incidents affecting many tenants, use severity-weighted adaptive sampling: sample more for tenants showing highest error rates and for routes matching rollout tag.
- Keep full payload traces only for up to 3 unique request_ids to limit PII and storage. Redact text fields where possible.

Investigation checklist (stepwise):
- [ ] Confirm alert validity (false positives from bad aggregation?).
- [ ] Compare canary vs baseline: identical synthetic inputs.
- [ ] Check routing/fallback rules: did traffic split change unexpectedly?
- [ ] Inspect pre-rollout model resource differences (quantized vs fp16 differences might change token speed).
- [ ] Look for infra events: node terminate/preempt, autoscaler flaps.
- [ ] If fallback counts up, inspect model artifact compatibility (tokenizer mismatch, model signature).
- [ ] If kv-cache misses spike, correlate with cache eviction metrics and GC windows.

Operator scripts / small CLI commands (notes for runbook):
- curl snapshots: curl -sS -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \"$REDWOOD_API/metrics/query?p=...\" - copy-paste query from snippets above.
- Force single-trace: curl -X POST $API/trace/debug -d '{"route":"/canary","force_trace":true, "reason":"incident OBS-xxx"}'

Communication checklist (what to post in Slack incident channel):
- Short TL;DR: what changed, top metric delta, immediate action taken (rollback / throttled / paused).
- Link to dashboard with time window pinned.
- Attach 1 representative trace (with sensitive content redacted).
- Post follow-up ETA for next update (every 15 minutes during active rollback).

Cost-aware probe policy (notes):
- Keep probes minimal during high-load windows. Prefer sampling and targeted probes to affected routes only.
- If investigating kv-cache warmth, prefer prefix-based probes that exercise cache warming over full synthetic corpus run.

Common failure patterns and heuristics (operator heuristics):
- sudden p95 spike + stable host CPU/GPU -> likely queuing or microburst in batch manager; check batch size distribution.
- p95 spike + increased container restarts -> runtime regressions (new kernel / compilation mismatch).
- increased fallback_count + changed model config -> compatibility/contract change (tokenizer or output schema).

Post-incident notes (what to capture before closing):
- Exact time window and model_version(s) affected.
- Representative trace ids (3) and which spans mapped to root cause.
- Probe results vs baseline.
- Action taken (rollback id, patch PR link).
- TODOs: instrumentation gaps discovered; add a dashboard widget to surface kvcache_eviction_rate by model.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we add an automated rollback trigger when model_variant p95 delta > 2x + fallback_rate > threshold? (risks: false positives)
- Investigate cheaper synthetic probe harness that replays actual user prefixes with privacy-safe masks.
- Add a small runbook UI button in Console to auto-collect 5 traces + snapshot metrics for an incident.

References and followups:
- Obs ticket for adding kvcache eviction metric: OBS-492 (linked above)
- Playbook PR to add rollback button: GH #27 (linked above)
- Short postmortem template: confluence.redwood.com/display/OBS/Incident+PM-Template

Notes to self (drafty):
- This doc should be converted into a Console-guided checklist if we see >3 incidents of this class in the next 6 weeks.
- Keep language short for oncall use — long narratives go in the PM.

-- end --
